claims.claim: More than one remodeler can simultaneously engage a promoter repeatedly over several minutes.
claims.source: Average time trace simulations of stably bound occupancies for each of the four remodelers over several hundred seconds (Figure 7B) show that at promoter regions targeted by multiple remodelers such as genes in 'cluster IV' enriched for RSC and INO80 (Kubik et al., 2019), the occupancy by any one remodeler is strikingly high, and more than one remodeler can simultaneously engage a promoter repeatedly over several minutes (Figure 7C; see also Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on simulations using measured kinetic parameters, as shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: All imaged remodelers show stable and transient residence times of 4–7 s and 0.4–0.7 s, respectively.
claims.source: Comparable to reported values for the Rsc2 subunit of RSC and the yeast transcription factors, Ace1 and Gal4 (Donovan et al., 2019; Mehta et al., 2018), all imaged remodelers show stable and transient residence times of 4–7 s and 0.4–0.7 s, respectively.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Donovan et al., 2019; Mehta et al., 2018.

claims.claim: The effect of mutating the DNA-binding domain of CHD1 monomer results in a threefold reduction in the τsb value (from 7.2 ± 3.3 to 2.4 ± 0.7 s).
claims.source: Furthermore, the effect of mutating the DNA-binding domain of CHD1 monomer (Ryan et al., 2011; Tran et al., 2000) results in a threefold reduction in the τsb value (from 7.2 ± 3.3 to 2.4 ± 0.7 s) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D and citations to Ryan et al., 2011; Tran et al., 2000.

claims.claim: Five tested ATPase-dead mutants (for ISW2, ISW1, CHD1) show twofold or greater increase in their stable-binding residence times.
claims.source: Importantly, the fast dissociation rates of remodelers are facilitated by ATP hydrolysis. Five tested ATPase-dead mutants (for ISW2, ISW1, CHD1) show twofold or greater increase in their stable-binding residence times (Figure 5C–F), highlighting a new role of for ATP-utilization in coupling nucleosome remodeling to rapid enzyme dissociation from chromatin.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C–F.

claims.claim: Remodelers undertake small translocation steps with remodeling rates of a few bp/sec.
claims.source: Biochemical studies have shown that remodelers undertake small translocation steps with remodeling rates of a few bp/sec (Blosser et al., 2009; Deindl et al., 2013; Harada et al., 2016; Qiu et al., 2017; Sabantsev et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blosser et al., 2009; Deindl et al., 2013; Harada et al., 2016; Qiu et al., 2017; Sabantsev et al., 2019.

claims.claim: With an enzymatic rate of 2 bp/s for ISWI, an ISWI stable-binding event would allow octamer sliding by roughly 12 bp.
claims.source: For example, with an enzymatic rate of 2 bp/s for ISWI (Blosser et al., 2009), an ISWI stable-binding event would allow octamer sliding by roughly 12 bp, which is within range of in vivo nucleosome position changes after conditional inactivation of RSC, SWI/SNF, INO80, and ISW2 (Ganguli et al., 2014; Kubik et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on cited enzymatic rates and is consistent with citations to Ganguli et al., 2014; Kubik et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Mutations in the ISW1, ISW2, and CHD1 Walker A motif substantially decreases in vivo mobility.
claims.source: We further showed that this enhanced mobility is dependent on the ATPase domain. Mutations in the ISW1, ISW2, and CHD1 Walker A motif implicated in nucleotide binding (Singleton et al., 2007) substantially decreases in vivo mobility.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Singleton et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Mutations in the CHD1 and ISW2 Walker B motif displays a milder decrease of its chromatin mobility.
claims.source: Further analysis of mutations in the CHD1 and ISW2 Walker B motif, implicated in ATP hydrolysis [but not ATP binding] (Singleton et al., 2007), displays a milder decrease of its chromatin mobility, suggesting that nucleotide binding is largely sufficient for promoting diffusion for the two remodelers.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Singleton et al., 2007.

claims.claim: RSC and Drosophila ISWI remodelers undergo ATP hydrolysis-dependent translocation on ssDNA and dsDNA in vitro.
claims.source: In addition, RSC and Drosophila ISWI remodelers undergo ATP hydrolysis-dependent translocation on ssDNA and dsDNA in vitro (Saha et al., 2005; Whitehouse et al., 2003), with processivities of 20–70 bp/translocation event (Fischer et al., 2007; Saha et al., 2005; Sirinakis et al., 2011; Whitehouse et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Saha et al., 2005; Whitehouse et al., 2003; Fischer et al., 2007; Sirinakis et al., 2011.

claims.claim: The absence of any change in ISW1 chromatin-bound mobility upon treatment with a general transcription inhibitor thiolutin rules out transcription per se as a source of enhanced remodeler diffusion.
claims.source: Finally, the absence of any change in ISW1 chromatin-bound mobility upon treatment with a general transcription inhibitor thiolutin rules out transcription per se as a source of enhanced remodeler diffusion (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Chromatin remodelers use the catalytic ATPase not only for nucleosome remodeling but also to enhance target search kinetics by promoting 1D diffusion on chromatin and rapid detachment after reaction.
claims.source: In all, our results suggest that chromatin remodelers use the catalytic ATPase not only for nucleosome remodeling but also to enhance target search kinetics by promoting 1D diffusion on chromatin and rapid detachment after reaction.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ATPase mutants and their effects on mobility and dissociation.

claims.claim: About half of promoters genome-wide harbor at least two distinct remodelers that harbor nucleosome pushing and pulling activities relative to the NDR.
claims.source: Yeast promoter regions can be classified into different groups enriched either for no remodeler or a combination of RSC, SWI/SNF, INO80, and ISW2, with about half of promoters genome-wide harboring at least two distinct remodelers that harbor nucleosome pushing and pulling activities relative to the NDR (Kubik et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kubik et al., 2019.

claims.claim: At promoter regions where opposing remodelers bind, a consecutive 'tug-of-war' between the pushing and pulling activities is expected.
claims.source: At promoter regions where opposing remodelers bind, we expect a consecutive 'tug-of-war' between the pushing and pulling activities, in which successive engagements would ultimately result in fine-tuning the steady-state nucleosome position, with the final outcome dependent on remodeler occupancy and nucleosome remodeling activity.
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data and known remodeler activities.

claims.claim: The average promoter occupancy of the yeast PIC is in the range of 10%.
claims.source: In a related study (Nguyen et al., 2021), the average promoter occupancy of the yeast PIC that forms upstream and overlapping the +1 nucleosome was found to be in the range of 10%, that is on the same order of magnitude but lower than three of four remodelers examined.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nguyen et al., 2021.

claims.claim: A full PIC lasts only several seconds before dissociation from chromatin.
claims.source: Similar to chromatin remodelers, a full PIC lasts only several seconds before dissociation from chromatin, but the average promoter is vacant for ~100 s before PIC reformation.
claims.evidence: This is a statement based on the related study mentioned (Nguyen et al., 2021).

claims.claim: The average promoter is vacant for ~100 s before PIC reformation.
claims.source: Similar to chromatin remodelers, a full PIC lasts only several seconds before dissociation from chromatin, but the average promoter is vacant for ~100 s before PIC reformation.
claims.evidence: This is a statement based on the related study mentioned (Nguyen et al., 2021).

claims.source: It is notable that an independent study from the Verrijzer laboratory (Tilly et al. 2021) found that the Drosophila Brahma (BRM) remodeler also displays dependence on ATP utilization by the catalytic ATPase for dynamic mobility and remodeler dissociation in live Drosophila cells.

results.result: HaloTag fusion proteins for six chromatin remodeling complexes were successfully generated and validated. The fusion proteins localized to the nucleus, showed no detectable tag cleavage, and exhibited no growth phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C24 provide converging evidence that the HaloTag fusion approach is functional. Nuclear localization (C22), lack of tag cleavage (C23), and absence of phenotypes (C24) collectively validate the experimental system for subsequent single-molecule tracking studies.

results.result: Chromatin remodelers exhibit distinct chromatin-bound and chromatin-free populations with varying binding fractions. Remodelers show 2-fold higher Dbound values than H2B and 10-fold higher Dfree values, with chromatin-binding fractions ranging from 35-66% across different remodeler families.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C40 present comprehensive fast-tracking data showing distinct diffusive populations for all six remodelers. The use of H2B and Halo-NLS as controls (C25-C26), consistent methodology across remodelers (C27-C36, C40), and correlation with molecular weight (C30) provide strong support for these measurements.

results.result: Chromatin remodelers display frequent transitions between chromatin-bound and free states. Transitioning trajectories represent 21-30% of remodeler molecules, significantly higher than H2B (7%) or free HaloTag (10%), with balanced frequencies of association and dissociation.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 are supported by vbSPT Hidden Markov Model analysis distinguishing bound, free, and transitioning populations. The higher transitioning frequency for remodelers compared to controls (C42), balanced directionality (C43), and validation of state assignments strengthen this conclusion (C44).

results.result: All six chromatin remodelers exhibit remarkably short chromatin residence times of 4-7 seconds for stable binding. Residence times were measured using slow-tracking and corrected for photobleaching using H2B as a reference.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 and C71 present consistent residence time measurements across all remodelers using slow-tracking methodology. The photobleaching correction using H2B, double exponential fitting to distinguish stable and transient binding, and consistency with prior measurements for RSC (C45) support these findings.

results.result: ATPase-dead mutants in the Walker A motif show 2-fold or greater increases in chromatin residence times. Five tested mutants (Isw2K215R, Isw1K227R, Chd1K407R, Chd1D513N, Isw2D312N) all exhibited slower dissociation rates compared to wildtype.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C55, C60, and C73 demonstrate that ATP hydrolysis facilitates rapid dissociation. Multiple independent mutants across three remodelers show consistent increases in residence time, with proper controls and consistency with prior biochemical studies (C55).

results.result: Chromatin-bound remodelers exhibit 2-fold higher mobility than H2B histone, and this enhanced mobility requires ATP binding but not necessarily ATP hydrolysis. Walker A mutants show reduced mobility while Walker B mutants show milder effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C59, C76-C77, and C79 provide strong evidence for ATP-dependent enhanced mobility. The differential effects of Walker A versus Walker B mutations (C58-C59, C76-C77) and control experiment ruling out transcription effects (C79) support the conclusion that ATP binding is sufficient for enhanced diffusion.

results.result: The catalytic ATPase has dual functions: nucleosome remodeling and enhancing target search kinetics through promoting 1D diffusion on chromatin and rapid detachment after reaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C61 and C80 synthesize findings from mobility and residence time experiments with ATPase mutants. The distinction between ATP binding (sufficient for mobility) and hydrolysis (required for rapid dissociation) is well-supported by the Walker A versus Walker B mutant data.

results.result: Chromatin remodelers show substantial temporal occupancies at target promoters ranging from 11-94%. RSC shows 30% occupancy, SWI/SNF 94%, INO80 25%, and ISW2 11%, calculated from measured kinetic parameters and literature values for molecule numbers and target sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C68 present occupancy calculations that depend critically on literature values for Nmolecules and Ntargets (C62-C64). While the kinetic measurements are well-supported, the occupancy calculations involve multiple assumptions and propagated errors. The large error bars (e.g., SWI/SNF: 94±41%) and reliance on external data sources introduce uncertainty.

results.result: Kinetic simulations based on measured parameters show that multiple remodelers can repeatedly and simultaneously occupy the same promoter region on a timescale of minutes, supporting a 'tug-of-war' model for nucleosome positioning.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C69-C70, and C82 present simulation results based on experimentally measured kinetic parameters. The simulations are appropriately grounded in the measured residence times and occupancy calculations, though the tug-of-war model (C82) remains somewhat speculative as it cannot be directly tested with the current data.

results.result: Mutation of the CHD1 DNA-binding domain results in a 3-fold reduction in stable-binding residence time (from 7.2±3.3 to 2.4±0.7 s).
results.evaluation: Claim C72 provides evidence that DNA-binding domains contribute to residence time. The measurement is consistent with the methodology used for other mutants and helps distinguish specific from non-specific binding.

results.result: Background information on chromatin structure, nucleosome organization, and remodeler classification and function is established through citations to prior literature.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C20, C37-C39, C62-C64, and C81 present established knowledge about chromatin biology supported by appropriate citations. These provide necessary context for interpreting the experimental results.

results.result: Biochemical studies show remodelers undertake small translocation steps with rates of a few bp/sec, and the measured 4-7 s residence times would allow ~12 bp of nucleosome sliding, consistent with in vivo position changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 and C78 integrate prior biochemical measurements with the current findings to provide mechanistic context. The calculation in C75 appropriately connects residence times to functional outcomes.

results.result: The yeast PIC shows ~10% promoter occupancy and lasts several seconds before dissociation, with ~100 s vacancy before reformation, based on a related study.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C85 cite a related study (Nguyen et al., 2021) to provide comparative context for remodeler occupancy. These are appropriately attributed to the cited work.

results.result: An independent study in Drosophila found that the BRM remodeler also shows ATP-dependent dynamic mobility and dissociation, supporting conservation of these mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claim C86 appropriately cites independent corroborating evidence from another system, strengthening the generalizability of the findings.

results.result: Chromatin remodelers establish genome-wide chromatin architectures, display higher diffusion than histones with 4-7 s residence times, and require ATP binding/hydrolysis for enhanced dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 from the abstract accurately summarize the major findings of the study. These are well-supported by the detailed experimental results presented in the manuscript.
